hub.intro: Pick your role and see what to buy first, what to add once a clear trigger hits, what to skip for now, and what the stack costs per month at the vendors' published prices.
hub.summary: Most CRE software is sold to newcomers in the wrong order: the big data subscription first, the boring system of record later. These stacks start with the tools that run the business day to day, many of them free or under $100 a month, and add the expensive ones only when a specific trigger makes them pay for themselves. Each role page names one or two honest alternatives for every slot, so you can swap a pick without losing the logic.
methods: Every price comes from the vendor's own pricing page, turned into a monthly figure. An annual price is divided by 12, and per-seat or per-unit prices are multiplied by the seats or units each role assumes. Every line shows that basis and the date we checked it.
Tools that are only sold by quote are still listed where they fit, labeled "pricing on request", and left out of the totals. A stack that includes them will cost more than the total shown.
When a vendor publishes only a starting price ("from" or "starting at"), we use that figure and mark the line and the total "from". Expect a higher quote as seats or units grow.
When a vendor's site blocked our automated check, we used the price in our own listing only where it is the vendor's published figure, and the line says it was not rechecked.

The lean total is everything under Start with. The fuller total adds every Add when tool and drops any starter tool it replaces. Totals exclude tax, payment processing, screening fees paid by applicants, onboarding and setup fees, and hardware.
This is desk research from vendor documentation and published pricing, not hands-on testing. No vendor pays for a place in these stacks.

faq.question: How much does a starter CRE software stack cost per month?
faq.answer: At published prices, a self-managing landlord with about 40 units or a first-time sponsor can start at {{lean:small-residential-landlord}} a month, and a solo commercial broker at {{lean:solo-commercial-broker}}. At the other end, a manager with 1,000 doors pays {{lean:growing-property-manager}} a month for the system of record alone, and its fuller stack costs {{full:growing-property-manager}} a month. Quote-only tools come on top of these figures.

faq.question: Why are some tools left out of the totals?
faq.answer: They do not publish prices. CoStar, Yardi Voyager, Juniper Square, ARGUS and most enterprise platforms are sold by quote, often by market, seat or portfolio size. We list them where they fit, label them pricing on request, and keep them out of the totals rather than guess.

faq.question: Are free tools really enough to start?
faq.answer: Often, yes. Free listing tiers, free rent estimates, free bookkeeping such as Stessa Essentials and free Excel underwriting models cover a surprising amount of a first year. Each role page says where a free tier is genuinely enough and what trigger tells you it no longer is.

faq.question: Is there a starter stack for CRE lenders and debt funds?
faq.answer: Not yet. Most loan origination, servicing and draw management software for commercial real estate is sold by quote only, so a cost total would be mostly blank. The CRE loan servicing and debt management buyer's guides cover that software in depth.

faq.question: How current are these prices?
faq.answer: Each line shows the date its price was last checked against the vendor's site, and the totals are rebuilt from those lines whenever the site is published. Vendors change plans often, so confirm the price on the vendor's page before you buy.

faq.question: What is the cheapest workable software setup for a solo commercial broker?

faq.question: Does a solo broker need CoStar?

faq.question: What does the fuller solo broker stack add?

faq.question: What software does a small land acquisition team need first?
faq.answer: A way to search parcels by zoning and reach owners, a phone app for parcel lines in the field, and a model you trust. At published prices, Plotzy Starter ($180/mo), LandGlide for two people ($16.67/mo billed annually) and the free A.CRE models come to {{lean}} a month, with Mastt's free plan for the first project budget.

faq.question: Is TestFit worth it for a small developer?
faq.answer: Once you test more than a couple of sites a month. Parking Solver is $195/mo with unlimited users; before that, a civil engineer's test fit on your best site may be the better spend. With TestFit, verified zoning searches and project controls, the fuller stack is {{full}} a month.

faq.question: Do I need Procore as a developer?
faq.answer: Usually not on the owner side. Procore is priced on annual construction volume and is typically the contractor's platform; owners get project access through the GC. Owner-side budget and payment tracking can live in a lighter tool.

faq.question: What software does a small commercial landlord need?
faq.answer: A system built for commercial leases, escalations and CAM recoveries. StrataFolio Essential is $210 a month billed annually at 30 suites, which is the whole lean stack at {{lean}}. DoorLoop and Yardi Breeze commercial are published alternatives with $199 and $200 monthly minimums.

faq.question: Can residential landlord software handle commercial leases?
faq.answer: Some can, but check CAM reconciliation, percentage rent and escalations before you commit. Tools built for single-family rentals often treat every lease as a fixed monthly rent, which is where commercial owners lose recoveries.

faq.question: What does the fuller commercial landlord stack add?
faq.answer: Work order software for two users (UpKeep Essential, $48 a month) once a building engineer or several vendors are involved, and stacking plans for brokers and lenders (Stackplanner Starter, $99 a month billed annually). Together that is {{full}} a month.

faq.question: What software does an acquisitions analyst at a small firm need?
faq.answer: Free Excel models such as the A.CRE library, a rent roll extractor (CRE Data Extractor Pro, $20/mo), rent comps (RentCast Pro, $12/mo billed annually) and owner records (PropertyShark Pro, $50/mo billed annually). That lean stack is {{lean}} a month at published prices.

faq.question: Do I need ARGUS to underwrite deals?
faq.answer: Only for multi-tenant office and retail where lenders and partners expect ARGUS cash flows. Multifamily and simple net lease deals are underwritten in Excel almost everywhere, and ARGUS pricing is quoted.

faq.question: What does the fuller analyst stack add?
faq.answer: Unit-level multifamily comps (HelloData Standard, $300 per user per month) in place of RentCast, and verified commercial lease comps from CompStak Enterprise, which is priced by quote and not totaled. The published-price total is {{full}} a month.
